Which creation each row waiting for an account shares

creation_shares.Rd

The rows absent that a round is about to create, and the name the resolution found free for each. The name is free when the round sweeps and taken once the first POST of it has made the account, so the round sends each name once, for the oldest row that waits for it. Age is the numeric record_id, as the oldest row of a repeated pair keeps it in register_to_desired(), and not the order of the export; without a record_id it is the order of the rows.

Usage

creation_shares(rows, upns)

Arguments

rows

The register rows, carrying record_id, first_name, last_name and contact_email.

upns

The name each row would be created under, as the resolution composed it.

Value

An integer vector, one per row: the position of the row whose creation it shares, its own when it makes one, and NA when it waits for the next round.

Details

The other rows that wait for the same name are one of two things. The same person asked for again, on another project: the same name and surname, as directory_named() folds them, and the same contact address. That row shares the creation, one account, one key and one welcome, and next round finds the account by the criterion the resolution uses and is created like the first. Or somebody else with the same name, or the same person with another address, which nothing in the round can tell apart: that row waits, and next round meets the new account as a namesake, ambiguous, which the referent and IT settle. Taking the next free name at once would make a second account for a person who may already have one.
